title: Mental Check
text: So doesn’t that mean I need to stop this fishing expedition in the first place? Even if I keep the wave damage to a minimum, I can’t stop the sea from getting rough, I say. Of course, there’s a chance the sea won’t get rough… but that’s about as uncertain as uncertain gets.

Come to think of it, earlier Trash was asking Éclair’s parent to go catch some rare fish since the Crimson Swine was coming home. That exchange between Trash and Éclair’s parent, regarding a letter, indeed. It seemed like the Crimson Swine wanted some rare fish dish prepared. The flow was that Trash got asked via letter, and then passed the request along.

The wave was caused by the Crimson Swine’s true body… and since the Crimson Swine itself seems to be its terminal, does that mean it arranged things so the damage would be worse? Crimson Swine… so you were claiming victims even in a place like this?

Anyway… it seems this village got dragged into an unplanned deep-sea fishing trip because of the Crimson Swine’s whim. Which means it’s set in stone that Older Sister, who has high combat ability, left the village because of that. I’m thinking about how to prevent them from setting sail at all, but worst case, I could just blast straight through all the ships to stop it, I say.

Hey now— in my head, Father and the others, not to mention Rabbit Guy, are giving me that look like I’m an idiot, but there’s no problem with this plan! I just need to smash the ships right before departure, indeed! “You’re way too muscle-brained, Motoyasu-kun…” I can almost hear gentle Father saying, but it’s the easy way out. If the sea’s going to be too rough to use them for a while anyway, it should be fine. Timing the destruction is the important part, though. Well, this one’s solved! And with that, one item checked off the mental list.

Next up, Éclair’s parent. This one’s also apparently caused by the fighting on the wave front. There’s a mansion in a neighboring town nearby. When this parent of Éclair’s died, apparently slave hunters flooded into this territory—which had been friendly ground for demi-humans—taking advantage of the chaos. On top of that, the Three Heroes Church colluded with Trash to push forward with enslaving demi-humans. Crocodile Guy got caught up in this too, I believe—his parent died and he himself ended up enslaved.

Setting that aside for now… Éclair’s parent dying is, in itself, a cause that accelerates Melromarc’s problems considerably. Of course, if I subdue the wave immediately, there’s a good chance they won’t die… but if I’m too active, I’ll draw too much attention. It’s not that I’m against acting as a hero, but Ren from the previous loop comes to mind. …That’s a bit unpleasant, I say. To begin with, if I’m too conspicuous, won’t the Three Heroes Church seize the opportunity to prop me up and push all sorts of troublesome schemes, like ordering me to attack Siltvelt?

As a result, they might even go so far as to assassinate Éclair’s parent as an obstacle. If that happens, we’re back to square one. Which means… it’d probably be better, thinking ahead, to subdue the wave while also acting in a way that makes me look less conspicuous. …Disguising myself as an usaunny might not be a bad idea either.
“This is all rather complicated, I say.”

Father, who stayed in Melromarc and was active in all sorts of ways, ended up with tremendous public support. I’d rather avoid ending up like that myself. If someone took Filolial-sama hostage to control me at will, I don’t think I could stand it, indeed.

…Hm? Did something like that actually happen? Hmm. I can’t quite recall. What an unpleasant possibility. But that’s something I absolutely do not want done to me. If possible, I’d like to maneuver things so no one tries that kind of stunt.

I really would like to arrange the environment so I draw as little attention as possible. This sort of thing is usually something I’d ask Father to handle… and the painful part is that there’s a high chance I won’t even be able to meet Father in the first place. Regardless, the priority for now should be avoiding the tragedies that befall Big Sister and the others, as well as Éclair. Thinking about it that way… while I’ll support from the shadows, it would be preferable to set up someone else as the valiant one who subdued the wave.

So… let me think about who among the people in this region could plausibly fill that role. It needs to be someone I know is here, someone with combat experience, and someone who survives after the wave. If they die in the wave, I should just conclude their ability wasn’t enough in the first place. The candidates who come to mind are Older Sister, and perhaps Éclair too, if I can subtly guide her here in time? And then… I believe Crocodile Guy is also around here, isn’t he? Older Sister was away on the fishing trip, Éclair was on duty at the castle, and Crocodile Guy was on-site but wasn’t strong enough and ended up enslaved after a surprise attack.

Older Sister is strong to begin with. If she’s present at the wave site, I think she’d perform well enough that there’d be no issue. Éclair is a bit of a concern. Crocodile Guy, needless to say, even more so. Should I capture them and forcibly drag them along?

But doing that risks arousing suspicion, not to mention unforeseen complications. If I pulled something like that, I’d be marked as suspicious instantly. If their guard goes up, it’ll be harder for me to move freely. In that case, it’s probably best to have Older Sister do the fighting. Across the many loops so far, this event has left Older Sister with considerable regret. If only she’d been there, at that place, at that time. It’d be best to set up Older Sister—someone who got along well with Big Sister and Father and lent her strength to them—as the hero of the hour. The problem is that Older Sister is quite observant, so there’s a chance she’ll notice me working behind the scenes.

For now… I need to find out when the fishing fleet is set to depart. That said, the fish Older Sister and the others bring back from deep-sea fishing—the whole freshness issue—that’s probably handled by freezing them with ice magic or something during transport, I’d guess. This is a world where, thanks to magic, the freshness problem is fairly well solved in general. Keeping myself hidden and eavesdropping continuously is an option, but that would be a waste of effort in its own way. Well, if I just check in on things daily, I should be able to get a rough idea of the timing. It’s not as though they’re operating in strict secrecy anyway.

Is this plan good enough to go with? There’s still a chance something else is lurking that I’m missing… but for now, let’s think about what else I can do. What should take priority right now? Something I can only do right now, precisely because of the timing.

Come to think of it… earlier there was talk of the Crimson Swine coming home. Something about a long school break or whatever. Since it was already present when we were summoned at the castle, it must have already returned by then… hmm. I believe I heard that we were summoned around two weeks or so before the wave occurred. Well, since the next wave was a month out, that timing checks out.

Storming into the Crimson Swine’s academy in Faubrey and secretly killing it might be an option, indeed. The question is how to do it. Since it causes all sorts of trouble, speed is of the essence. Right. Let’s go find the Crimson Swine and finish it off. …? I feel like I’m forgetting something, but… well, there’s no use worrying about it now. And so, I’m off to Faubrey right away, I say.
“Portal Spear!”
Fwoosh! And with that, I arrived at the Faubrey portal point I’d set up in advance.

Same cultured, sophisticated country as ever. Well, with no wave damage here, there’s nothing much changed about the place. Thinking such thoughts, I infiltrate the academy where the Crimson Swine is supposedly enrolled, using knowledge from a past loop.
“Oink-oink.”
“Oink-oink-oink.”
“Ahh, I’m exhausted, I don’t wanna do club activities today.”

That sort of nostalgic school scenery echoed through the school building. Of course, I infiltrated in stealth mode. I could have disguised myself, but there was no need. Come to think of it, Faubrey’s schools do have a fair number of demi-humans and beastmen enrolled, I say. Though it’s located a bit away from Faubrey’s capital. The Sage is also enrolled here, though I believe he didn’t attend very often. As for Takt… had he already graduated by this point? I think I heard somewhere that the Crimson Swine and Riska were in the same year. Thinking all this, I searched around the academy… but where on earth was the Crimson Swine? I was hunting for a room and a spot to carry out the killing, but couldn’t find it anywhere. Asking around would be one option, but having my crime noticed afterward would be a hassle. So, I ended up fumbling my way through the dormitory, searching room by room, until the sun had completely set.
Grr… I can’t tell the Crimson Swine apart from the rest! Wasn’t this just a blunder, a complete waste of time?
